A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on the noisy logistic map, ordered MNIST, Langevin dynamics, and chignolin, including numerical results and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds chignolin scalability, orthogonality, and training-stability results.

M1.justification: The LoRA objective, constant-mode handling, joint and sequential nesting, continuous-time formulation, and CCA/EDMD inference procedures are retained. Uniform nesting weights already appear in v1's pseudocode. The new batch-normalization removal is an experimental ablation, not a replacement of the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same four benchmark domains and tasks, including the same 300 K chignolin data. The noisy logistic map moves to Appendix G.1. New chignolin experiments vary model and training configurations within retained coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparison methods remain VAMPnet, DPNet, DPNet-relaxed, and its centered variant where applicable. The unsuccessful Langevin DPNet comparison and centered chignolin baseline already appear in v1. Newly discussed concurrent methods are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v2 introduces an eight-configuration chignolin sweep over mode count, SchNet width, and batch size, normalized-Gram evaluation, and a 200-epoch test without final batch normalization. It also resolves v1's Langevin main-text k=10 versus appendix top-8 inconsistency to top-10 and drops normalization from the stated postprocessing. These reporting revisions do not establish that the retained Langevin experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: New chignolin analyses test scalability and stability across configurations (Table 3), basis orthogonality on training and test data (Figure 5), and whether nesting stabilizes training without final batch normalization (Figure 6). These substantially expand the optimization diagnostics. The earlier sensitivity and folding-correlation analyses remain.

E5.justification: Existing benchmarks retain their five- or ten-run information and standard-deviation conventions. v2 explicitly identifies the new scalability table and Gram analysis as using seed 0, while the new stability curves provide no repeated-run uncertainty. This adds limited seed-reporting information without establishing an increase in repeated runs.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial scaling, orthogonality, and normalization-ablation results. For example, Table 3 reports VAMP-E scores of 31.61 for LoRAseq, -9.76 for DPNet-relaxed, and 5.20 for its centered variant at (k,H,B)=(64,128,384). The original benchmark plots, VAMP-2 scores, five-split VAMP-E scores, folding correlations, and numerical timescale estimates are retained.

T1.justification: The LoRA optimality statement, concentration bound, finite-rank SVD/eigenanalysis proofs, and EDMD derivations remain after appendix reordering. v2 removes the auxiliary underdamped-Langevin transition-path-time formula and parameter assumptions in v1 Appendix G.4.3, together with the associated timescale calculations and justification in G.4.4.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal contributions remain scalable LoRA-based learning of top-k Koopman singular functions, avoidance of unstable training operations, and support for eigenanalysis and multistep prediction. The conclusion retains the broad superiority and scalability claims; the added experiments support those existing claims.

C2.justification: v1 acknowledges microsecond relaxation processes but nevertheless validates nanosecond estimates against a 40±10 ns transition-path reference. v2 abandons that justification, calls the estimates model-dependent lower bounds, and requests multiple-lag-time validation. LoRAjnt's unchanged 71.3 ns estimate is consequently presented favorably as the longest estimate rather than an overestimate. New discussion also links orthogonality and nesting to stability.

D1.justification: v1 promises code release upon acceptance; v2 reports a public implementation and supplies its URL. Appendix G.4.1 and new Table 5 disclose SchNet components, architectural hyperparameters, explicit training settings, regularization strength, and force-field selection details previously largely delegated to prior work. These are substantial reproducibility disclosures, not evidence of a changed primary architecture.

R1.justification: Appendix A.2 substantially expands methodological positioning through historical LoRA references, density-ratio estimation, spectral representation learning, Turri et al.'s concurrent evolution-operator method and its parameterization, and neural orbital minimization. References supporting the removed transition-path rationale, including Laleman, Morozova, and Satoh, disappear. These changes extend beyond bibliographic corrections.

P1.justification: v2 reorganizes notation and preliminary methods into numbered subsections, restructures inference, moves the noisy-logistic-map experiment to the appendix, and reorders the technical appendices. It also substantially rewrites the chignolin discussion and conclusion. This is a broad narrative and structural revision beyond the added scientific content.

P2.justification: v2 adds scalability and architecture tables (Tables 3 and 5), Gram-matrix heatmaps (Figure 5), and a training-stability plot (Figure 6). The original logistic-map figure moves to the appendix, and the timescale figure is redrawn and repositioned without the 40±10 ns reference band. Existing result tables are retained and renumbered where necessary.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially improves the credibility of the chignolin case study by withdrawing v1's problematic validation of relaxation times against a transition-path-time reference and explicitly acknowledging unresolved slower folding dynamics. Added scaling and stability evidence strengthens the previously broad scalability claim, while the reported code release and detailed configuration improve reproducibility. Single-seed scalability results and the absence of multiple-lag-time validation still limit the conclusions, but the overall gains are substantial.
